bounded_statement: Within the supplied files only: the report's selected statistical conclusion (Welch t = 2.874, df = 45.7, p < 0.01, 'significant at alpha = 0.05') is obtained by entering all four nubbin rows of each of the 12 colonies as separate observations (n = 24 per zone) into Welch's two-sample t-test, a procedure that assumes independent rows, even though the data description designates colony_id as the independent unit. Recomputing the same Welch test on the 12 colony means (n = 6 per zone) yields the same mean difference (0.305) but t ≈ 1.35, df ≈ 10, p ≈ 0.21, so the claimed significance is not supported at the declared independent-unit level.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about its unit handling: it discloses that every nubbin record contributed one observation, so the repeated entry is not concealed. This mitigates concerns of misreporting but does not make the significance claim valid.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defend the report in three ways. (1) Checked for a computation error that might explain the result instead: recomputing the row-level Welch test by hand from the CSV gives means 1.833 vs 1.528, SDs 0.382 and 0.353, t = 0.305/sqrt(0.382^2/24 + 0.353^2/24) ≈ 2.87, matching the reported 2.874 — the code faithfully implements what the report describes, so the result is fully attributable to the unit choice, not a bug. (2) Tested whether the conclusion is robust to correct unit handling: aggregating to the 12 colony means (lagoon: 2.10, 1.55, 2.42, 1.28, 1.94, 1.71; forereef: 1.62, 1.19, 2.05, 1.40, 1.08, 1.83) and rerunning Welch's test gives the same mean difference 0.305 but SE ≈ 0.226, t ≈ 1.35, Welch df ≈ 10, two-sided p ≈ 0.21 — not significant, so the p < 0.01 claim does not survive. (3) Considered whether nubbins could plausibly be treated as independent despite the description: the data contradict this — within-colony spreads (~0.03–0.07) are an order of magnitude smaller than the spread of colony means (~0.40), indicating near-total within-colony correlation, and the description explicitly designates colony_id as the independent unit. All three defenses fail, confirming the issue.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py's read_densities() appends every CSV row's symbiont_density_e6_per_cm2 into a flat per-zone array with no aggregation or modeling of colony_id, and build_report() passes those 24-element arrays directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind(..., equal_var=False). Because each colony supplied four nubbins that are near-duplicates (within-colony SD ≈ 0.03–0.07 vs between-colony SD of colony means ≈ 0.40), each independent unit enters the row-independent t-test four times, inflating the per-group sample size from 6 to 24 and the degrees of freedom from ~10 to ~46, which manufactures the p < 0.01 result.
